comment: Decisions about what the token package says of the theme's roles. Every section here depends on
the package, so jest does not compare them - a token bump must not turn CI red. tools/review/roles.mjs
reads this file:
--report=<this file> - what moved against these rows: new, gone, changed, undecided. Never fails.
--write=<this file>  - re-stamps every section from the current run, keeping decision/why by key.
tokens:update prints the report after a bump. tests/roles.test.ts only checks that every row here
carries a decision from its vocabulary and a reason.
open - every role the package disagrees with, and what was decided about it.
verdict   cross-family   - the package uses this role, but only for a slot of another kind
family-conflict - the package paints this slot from another family entirely
decision  confirmed   - the package assigns this very role here; only our slot word differs
naming      - the role is right for what the property paints; the slot word is not
rule-5      - one value in two roles, named after the dominant one (DIVERGENCES)
bridge      - built with rgb(from role / a); the foundation names no role for it
package-gap - no role of the right family exists; a request, not a swap
design      - a correction would move a pixel, so it is not ours to make
rungs - our role is the one the package names for another state of the same slot.
contrast - foreground and background the bundle puts in ONE rule, resolved per mode. Alpha-bridge
values and disabled selectors are excluded: the first renders as a tint over an unknown surface,
the second is exempt from WCAG 1.4.3 and gated by disabled-paint.test.ts. decision graphic-ok means
the pair is a glyph and clears 3:1; design means it misses the threshold that applies to it.

NAMING decides the SLOT WORD from the property, so the name keeps -bg (it paints background-color) and only the role family follows what the element is. Same judgment call, and the same wording, as check-box-invalid-mark-bg. Value-neutral: primary-shared is one value across bg, border and content. Banked by D21

rungs.name: button-danger-outlined-content
rungs.why: The outlined and text buttons keep the hue on the label at rest; the package puts a neutral `content` there and brings the hue in only when the button is selected. Opened as D17 and answered by the designer on 16.09: keep the tinted look, move only the two rungs that failed contrast. So the rung difference is the decision, not a defect.

rungs.name: card-view-card-bg-selected
rungs.why: The package assigns exactly this role to exactly this thing; only the rung word differs, because it names the card's own `selected` state where we name the element `card-bg-selected`. Nothing to reconcile.

rungs.name: chat-avatar-bg
rungs.why: Measured before deciding: against the chat surface every neutral RESTING fill the system offers reads 1.04-1.09 - bg 1.00, bg-canvas 1.04, bg-low and bg-high 1.09 - because in light they are all #f5f5f5-#fafafa on #ffffff. The only neutral fills a disc is visible on are the state rungs: bg-selected 1.21 and bg-active 1.31, which is what the avatar reads today. So this is not a rung chosen carelessly but a role the design system does not ship: a resting neutral disc. Kept, and raised as a request to the package team.

rungs.name: check-box-icon-bg-disabled
rungs.why: The package paints `color-none` on a disabled box - it leaves it unfilled and lets the border carry the state - and uses content-disabled at read-only instead. We fill it. A different anatomy, not a different role: the disabled paint has its own gate here (tests/disabled-paint.test.ts).

rungs.name: gantt-selection-bg
rungs.why: Our element IS the selection, so its name carries no `-selected` suffix; the package reaches the same paint as the `selected` rung of a row. Same role, same paint, different spelling.

rungs.name: gantt-ti-bg
rungs.why: The band marking a time interval reads bg-primary-alpha-hovered, alpha 0.20. The resting rung of the same ramp is 0.11 and legacy fluent drew this band at 0.15, so neither rung is the legacy density and the rest rung is the fainter of the two: against the canvas the band goes from 1.33 to 1.16. Kept at the stronger rung and recorded in DIVERGENCES.md. Noted while measuring: the same ramp is read off-rung in two more places and in both directions - htmlEditor's variable chip is another resting element on the hovered rung, and the scheduler's FOCUSED cell reads the resting rung. That is a ramp-wide question, not this row.

rungs.name: grid-ai-chat-empty-icon-bg
rungs.why: Answered 17.09 by moving the disc to the rest rung of its own ramp, bg-primary-subtler: the glyph on it goes from 4.02 to 4.64 in light and 4.11 to 4.79 in dark, so the pair leaves the contrast list altogether. The row stays here because the package's grid names that role for a SELECTED row and has no empty-state badge at all - a difference of anatomy, with no rung of theirs left to agree with.

rungs.name: grid-cell-modified-bg

rungs.name: grid-selection-bg

rungs.name: scrollable-bg
rungs.why: The package leaves its scroll surface unpainted at rest (`color-none`) and gives it a background only on hover. Ours is an opaque surface under the content, which is a different element rather than a different rung.

rungs.name: slider-element-bg
rungs.why: Same as scrollable-bg: the package paints nothing at rest.

rungs.name: slider-tooltip-content
rungs.why: The package tints the slider tooltip label by hue and keeps neutral `content` for the hovered rung; our tooltip is one neutral label in every state, which is the tooltip we ship, not a rung of theirs.

rungs.name: tabs-tab-content-selected
rungs.why: Answered 17.09 as D37, option (2). A selected tab used to underline itself in the accent, colour its icon in the accent and leave its label neutral - the two halves of one element disagreeing. The icon joins the label on `content`, so the accent now marks a selected tab in exactly one place, the underline, and both rows sit here for the same reason: the package colours label and icon with content-primary-shared at that rung and we mark the tab by its selector instead. Values: the icon moves #0f6cbd to #161616 in light and #4b90d9 to #ffffff in dark; the underline is untouched.

rungs.name: text-editor-border-focused
rungs.why: Measured in the bundle: the accent line the package calls `text-input.line.focused = content-primary` is our `$text-editor-indicator`, which reads exactly `content-primary`. What our `-border-focused` and `-line-focused` paint is the box's own edge underneath that indicator. The role is right; the slot word `line` means a different line on each side.

rungs.name: tree-view-content
rungs.why: The package's tree item is `content-subtle` at rest and darkens to `content` on hover; ours is full `content` throughout. A deliberate contrast-positive difference, and moving to their ladder would lower the resting contrast of every tree label.

contrast.why: the drop separator of the group panel: a 2px bar in bg-primary, a graphic with a 3:1 floor, and 3.36 clears it. The panel's caption sits beside the bar, not on it. Surfaced by D23, not moved by it

Widened 09.09 after asking whether danger passes anywhere else. It does not, and the reason is that the role is tuned to one surface. In dark content-danger was danger-80 #e4554f, and it measured 4.58 on the page canvas (bg-canvas #1d1d1d), 4.22 on an ordinary surface (bg #242424) and 3.05 on a hovered one (bg-hovered #3b3b3b). So it cleared AA on the canvas by 0.08 and failed everywhere below it. Eleven theme variables put real text on this role - the outlined danger button label, the chat alert list, the chat delete item, the fieldset invalid value, the grid AI error, the informer error, two stepper invalid labels, the text editor invalid message, the validation message and the validation summary - and every one of them sat at 4.22 wherever its widget has its own background. Three more read the role for a glyph (diagram, filterBuilder, cardView), where 4.22 clears the 3:1 that applies. The request split in two: on an ordinary surface the miss was 0.28 and one ramp step fixes it - danger-70 #ee726a gives 5.36 - so we asked the package to move content-danger in dark; on a hovered surface nothing in the family clears AA, danger-70 reaching only 3.87, so that half stayed a genuine gap. Design tokens 262.26.0 made the requested move (dark content-danger is now danger-70), so the hovered-surface number moves from 3.05 to the 3.87 already anticipated above - still short of AA, so the decision stands as package-gap. Light is fine throughout (6.07 on the canvas, 5.56 hovered). Why the audit saw one row and not twelve: the rule-local pass needs both colours in one rule, and a validation message takes its background from an ancestor. Third instance of that blind spot in one day.

comment: Contrast measured across a state change - added 09.09.2026, and it is what the rest of this file
could not see. The rule-local pass needs a foreground and a background in one rule; a state
ladder never writes them together, so the states where a value actually moves were exactly the
blind spot. Exact equality: a row leaving or entering this list is a decision, not a ratchet.
threshold: 4.5 where the foreground is a label, 3 where it is a glyph or a boundary (WCAG 1.4.11).

checkbox-focused-fill.why:
Resolved in part on 15.09, when the designer produced the package tokens for checkbox/color/checked. Three slots, not one: border, bg and icon each have their own token, and our theme painted the border from the BG variable. Figma and Blazor agree that the border is border-primary-shared*, so that half was not a judgement call and is applied - three new names, light pixel-identical (primary-100/120/140 exactly as before), dark better at every rung: the box outline against the page goes 2.88 -> 4.65 at rest, 3.69 -> 5.79 hovered, 1.39 -> 1.98 pressed.
WHAT REMAINS. The fill. Figma says bg-primary*, Blazor implements content-primary-shared*, and the two are identical in light and differ in dark - which is exactly what decides this row. On Figma's fill the mark reads 3.36 at rest and 1.62 pressed; on Blazor's, 5.42 and 2.31. Neither clears 3.0 in the pressed state, because no primary family inverts its active rung for dark - the same package defect P2 records for danger.
AND A THIRD THING THE TOKENS SETTLE. The package state list is rest / hovered / active / read-only / disabled - there is no focused. Our theme paints .dx-state-focused AND .dx-state-active from one variable, so a keyboard user SITS at the value the package intends for a transient press. The button already separates them (bg-focused reads bg-primary-hovered). Splitting focus from active would leave the 1.62 where the package put it - under a finger, for the length of a click - and take the keyboard user to 4.30.
RE-CHECKED 15.09 against a freshly pulled Blazor, and the stem argument above was WRONG. Blazor's checked fills are content-primary-shared for primary but bg-success-shared and bg-danger-shared for the other two - I had read the INDETERMINATE variables, where the dash is a content-coloured mark, as the checked fills. So primary is the outlier inside Blazor, our bg family agrees with their success and danger, and our invalid MARK on content-danger-shared agrees with their indeterminate mark. There was no internal inconsistency.
WHICH LEAVES A CANDIDATE THAT SATISFIES BOTH SOURCES: bg-primary-shared*. The whole *-shared family is one value across bg, border and content, so it measures exactly like Blazor's content-primary-shared - mark 5.42 at rest and box 4.65 in dark against 3.36 and 2.88 today - while staying in the bg family Figma names, on the stem Blazor itself uses for success and danger. Light is identical to what ships now. The pressed rung still fails (2.31 / 1.98): no primary family inverts its active step for dark, which is P2's defect again.
RESOLVED 15.09, option 1. Focus now takes the HOVERED rung and the press keeps the package's active one, which is the shape the contained button already had (bg-focused reads bg-primary-hovered, bg-active reads bg-primary-active). The package state list justifies it: there is no focused state in it at all, so painting focus with the value meant for a click was never what the tokens asked for.
Four variables: -bg-focused and -border-focused moved down a rung, and -bg-active and -border-active were added to hold what the package assigns. The row that measured 1.62 split in two - the press keeps 1.62 on a state that lasts as long as a finger is down, and the focus a keyboard user SITS in went to 4.30, over the 3:1 a glyph needs. Light moves one step on focus, #003c70 -> #005397. Cascade verified on eight combinations: checked rest, hover, focus and press, the invalid pair, and the indeterminate pair including its ::before dash.
The fill STEM question is untouched and still open: bg-primary* as it ships, against bg-primary-shared* which reads 5.42 / 4.65 in dark where today it is 3.36 / 2.88.
STEM ACCEPTED 15.09. The checked fill moved from the plain bg-primary family to bg-primary-shared*. Light is pixel-identical at every rung - primary-100, 120, 120, 140 exactly as before - because the plain and shared families coincide in light. Dark improves everywhere: rest primary-100 -> 80, hovered and focused 90 -> 70, press 140 -> 120. The rest row left the contrast list (3.36 -> 5.42), hovered and focused left the state-pair list (4.30 -> 6.75), and the press went 1.62 -> 2.31 - still under 3, because the package gives no primary family an inverted active rung, which is P2 again.
Why the stem matters at all: the plain family does not know the mode. bg-primary is #0f6cbd in BOTH modes and bg-primary-active #003c70 in both, while the mark on them, content-inverted, does flip - to #161616 in dark. A fixed fill under a flipping mark is what produced 3.36 and 1.62. Every rung of the shared family flips.
CLOSED 15.09. All three parts are applied - the outline has its own role, focus is separated from the press, and the fill is on the shared stem. What is left below the floor is the press at 2.31 in dark, and no shipped role fixes it: every primary family keeps its active rung un-inverted for dark. That is the same package defect P2 files for danger, so it leaves the theme as a report rather than a question.

contained-button-label.why:
The filled default and success buttons, and the completed stepper indicator, put a white label on bg-<hue>-hovered and land at 4.18-4.21 in dark against the 4.5 a label needs. Light is 7.5-7.8, so this is dark-only. The foreground is content-static-dark, which is #ffffff in both modes by design, so the whole movement is in the fill: bg-primary in dark is #0f6cbd giving 5.38, and its hovered rung lightens to #2b7ecf giving 4.21. A hover that lightens is correct for dark; it is the amount that overshoots. Nothing in the theme can fix this - the pair is two package roles used exactly as intended - so this is a report to the design system, alongside the danger-content row already filed. Listed as a question only to confirm we file it rather than swap a role.
CLOSED 15.09: handed to the designers and left as it is. Nothing in the theme can move it - the pair is two package roles used exactly as intended - so the theme carries it as a known report rather than an open question.

comment: Counted from the package inward: roles the four component sets assign that the theme reads
nowhere. capability - the role exists in the semantic layer and we simply never reached for it;
stale - the neighbours reference a name no layer declares, which is their drift, not our gap.
Exact equality: a role leaving this list means the theme started using it, which is a decision.

262.23.0 dropped two roles it used to declare and nobody read - color-border-contrast-disabled and color-content-active. The list is two shorter not because the theme started reading them but because they are gone from the package. Noticed while rebasing onto the base carrying that bump, 15.09.
